title: Timber! How Timber Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore timber and forestry in the United States and beyond. They cover forest definitions (forest vs. timberland, the ten percent tree cover and twenty cubic feet per acre per year thresholds), US forest acreage and the net annual increase in growing stock, regional hardwood and softwood divisions, and the uses of wood from fuel and construction lumber to paper, pulp, MDF, particle board and OSB. The hosts explain wood cell structure (cellulose and lignin), tree anatomy (bark, xylem, cambium, sapwood and heartwood), and the logging process from cruising and felling through bucking, skidding, landing areas and sawmills. They debate clear cutting versus selective and shelterwood methods, discuss the Mexican spotted owl and the shift of logging to the eastern US, greenwashing concerns about the Sustainable Forestry Initiative versus the Forest Stewardship Council, the Alaska Big Thorn timber sale, and invasive species such as the Eurasian gypsy moth, sudden oak death and kudzu. The episode ends with listener mail about a Ouija board tattoo.

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor
segments.summary: Hosts open with Squarespace sponsor read, Jerry's cold, and a playful intro about forests, then set up the topic of timber in North America.

segments.title: Forest acreage and definitions
segments.summary: Discussion of pre-settlement North American forest cover, the forest definition (one acre with at least ten percent tree cover), US forest acreage, and timberland as a forest with usable timber, including the twenty cubic feet per acre per year threshold.

segments.title: Net annual increase and regional forest types
segments.summary: Hosts explain net annual increase, note the US has been in annual gain for decades, credit early conservationists, and describe forest classification and the hardwood east and softwood west divide.

segments.title: Why wood is good: uses, carbon, habitat, water
segments.summary: Hosts cover long human use of wood including fire, the ecological value of forests for carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat and the water cycle, and indoor wood fuel health issues.

segments.title: Lumber and wood product breakdown
segments.summary: Breakdown of US timber use: about seven percent fuel, about fifty-three percent lumber, mostly for construction, pallets, crates and furniture, and the difference between lumber and roundwood, with a note on softwood vs hardwood for construction.

segments.title: Paper, pulp, fiberboard and composites
segments.summary: Explains wood cell structure with cellulose and lignin, making pulp and paper, and the differences between fiberboard, MDF, hardboard, particle board, plywood and oriented strand board.

segments.title: Harvesting methods: clear cutting vs. silviculture
segments.summary: Describes timber harvesting approaches: clear cutting (typically over five acres) versus silviculture methods such as shelterwood, seed tree and selection harvesting, and the debate over clear cutting, including seven conditions cited as justifying it.

segments.title: Felling a tree and the logging process
segments.summary: Cruising the forest, the felling process with a face cut, back cut and holding wood as described by forest fire manager Gabriel Fribley, followed by bucking, skidding trails, landing areas and concentration yards.

segments.title: Logging job safety
segments.summary: Discussion of logging being among the most dangerous US jobs, with commercial fishing, airline pilots, farmers, roofers and truckers also cited, and jokes about podcasting risk.

segments.title: Sawmill processing and tree anatomy
segments.summary: Debarking, the bark, xylem and cambium layers, sapwood versus heartwood, the reclaimed cypress from Florida swamps, knots, the chipper and digester for paper, and the scragg or head rig and edger for lumber, then kiln drying.

segments.title: Deforestation history and the Mexican spotted owl
segments.summary: Describes deforestation from the seventeenth to mid-nineteenth century, the fear of a wood famine, federal forest management, and the Mexican spotted owl endangered listing that shifted logging east.

segments.title: Certification and greenwashing
segments.summary: Hosts discuss forest certification labels, with the Sustainable Forestry Initiative accused of greenwashing by Forest Ethics and the Forest Stewardship Council seen as legitimate, plus companies shifting purchases.

segments.title: Alaska timber sale and invasive species
segments.summary: Covers the Big Thorn timber sale of old growth in the Tongass, the lawsuits, and threats from the Eurasian gypsy moth, sudden oak death and kudzu.

segments.title: Listener mail: Ouija board tattoo
segments.summary: A listener named Carrie writes in praising the Satanic Panic episode and sharing a photo of her Ouija board tattoo.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give contact info for Facebook, Twitter, email and the website and close the episode.
